source_excerpts.text:
### New theorem: donor concentration tuning has a spectral selectivity limit

Suppose several differently programmed molecules are simultaneously ready for different donors. Define \\(k\_{ij}\\) as the effective irreversible reaction-rate coefficient of donor \\(j\\) on a molecule that actually requires donor \\(i\\).

If all donor species are continuously present at fixed positive concentrations, the correct reaction hazard for programme \\(i\\) is \\(k\_{ii}c_i\\), and its incorrect reaction hazard is \\(\sum\_{j\ne i}k\_{ij}c_j\\).

Define

\\[ M\_{ij}= \begin{cases} k\_{ij}/k\_{jj},&i\ne j,\\\ 0,&i=j. \end{cases} \\]

For an irreducible nonnegative matrix \\(M\\), I obtain the exact minimax identity

\\[ \boxed{ \inf\_{c_i>0}\ \max_i \frac{\sum\_{j\ne i}k\_{ij}c_j}{k\_{ii}c_i} =\rho(M) } \\]

where \\(\rho(M)\\) is the spectral radius.

The proof uses the Collatz–Wielandt characterization of the Perron eigenvalue. This is an application of established mathematics, not a claim to have discovered a new spectral theorem.

The consequence is significant for Astra: if the measured cross-reaction matrix has too large a spectral radius, changing donor concentrations cannot make every simultaneously active programme sufficiently selective.

However, this limitation applies to stationary shared mixtures. It does not rule out changing the order of donor exposure.

SHARED MIXTURES AND ORDERED SUCCESS PROTECTION
For positive diagonal chemical coefficients k_ii, put x_i=k_ii*c_i. The ratio of incorrect to correct hazards becomes(Mx)_i/x_i with M_ij=k_ij/k_jj fori!=j and0 diagonal. For an irreducible nonnegative M, Collatz–Wielandt gives inf over positive concentrations of the maximum ratio=rho(M); the positive Perron vector realizes it. This is established linear algebra applied at a stationary shared-mixture interface. It is not an optimum of a finite-time damage/carryover programme, nor a measured matrix. Reducible zero patterns need their own attainment treatment.
If successful additions become protected and the unfinished setS is perfectly observed, the memoryless model has constant competing hazards while waiting for the next event. At a pure donorj, the correct-event contribution is k_jj*V(S\j); the denominator charges that success, wrong intended chemistryw_j, wrong reactions on all other unfinished lineages and their damage. Under the declared fixed total exposure normalization, a mixture's Bellman ratio is a ratio of affine positive combinations and is bounded by its best pure vertex. Induction on|S| yields the stated optimal pure-donor feedback recurrence. This does not acquire the perfect success observer or make arbitrary open-loop schedules optimal. Pure schedules can exploit asymmetric wrong chemistry because already successful lineages are protected; a directed cycle can retain a penalty even with ideal observation. The source's numeric optimizations/randomized comparison totals have missing original programs/results and remain source reports, not newly reconstructed numerical acceptance.
An unavoidable whole-product hazard d overL required cycles of durationT gives survival<=exp(-dTL), even when correct chemistry is arbitrarily fast. Carryover concerns ACTIVE donor, not inactive bound PNA mass. Persistent molecular competence must be averaged after each molecule's whole-programme probability, not redrawn each pulse; the two distributions give different joint laws. These simple models expose costs without establishing measured chemical rates or manufacturing performance.
